question: What is a converter dolly?
choice_a: A single-axle braking unit used only on triple trailers
choice_b: A coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel by which a semitrailer can be coupled to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination, forming a double bottom rig
choice_c: A device that connects the tractor's fifth wheel directly to the last trailer's kingpin, bypassing the middle trailer
choice_d: A hydraulic lift used only to raise a trailer's landing gear
explanation: The excerpt defines a converter dolly as a coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel that couples a semitrailer to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination to form a double bottom rig.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-1

question: Before backing a converter dolly under a rear trailer, what must be true about the trailer's height?
choice_a: It must be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel, so the trailer is raised slightly when the dolly is pushed under
choice_b: It must be exactly level with the dolly frame
choice_c: It must match the tractor's frame height exactly
choice_d: It must be raised as high as possible before the dolly approaches
explanation: The manual states the trailer height must be checked to be correct: slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel, so the trailer is raised slightly when the dolly is pushed under.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-1

question: When making a visual check of a converter dolly coupling to a trailer, what should a driver look for?
choice_a: That there is no visible space between the upper and lower fifth wheel and that the locking jaws are closed on the kingpin
choice_b: That the trailer brakes are fully released
choice_c: That the landing gear crank handle has been removed
choice_d: That the safety chains have been disconnected
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to make a visual check of coupling: no space between upper and lower fifth wheel, and locking jaws closed on the kingpin.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-1

question: While charging trailer brakes and checking for air at the rear of the second trailer by opening the emergency line shut-off, what does it mean if air pressure isn't there?
choice_a: The dolly must be uncoupled immediately before proceeding further
choice_b: Something is wrong, and the brakes won't work
choice_c: The trailer is simply empty of cargo
choice_d: The tractor protection valve has tripped normally as designed
explanation: The manual states that if air pressure isn't there when checking at the rear of the second trailer, something is wrong and the brakes won't work.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-1

question: During the procedure to uncouple the rear trailer of twin trailers, why is the landing gear of the second semitrailer lowered before pulling the dolly out?
choice_a: To disconnect the electrical cord more easily
choice_b: To make room to chock the wheels
choice_c: To remove some weight from the dolly
choice_d: To raise the trailer height for a final inspection
explanation: The excerpt instructs lowering the landing gear of the second semitrailer enough to remove some weight from the dolly, as one of the steps in uncoupling the rear trailer.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-2

question: According to the manual, why should a driver never unlock the pintle hook while the converter dolly is still under the rear trailer?
choice_a: It will cause the trailer brakes to lock automatically
choice_b: It causes permanent damage to the kingpin
choice_c: The dolly tow bar may fly up, possibly causing injury and making it very difficult to re-couple
explanation: The manual warns that unlocking the pintle hook with the dolly still under the rear trailer can cause the dolly tow bar to fly up, possibly causing injury and making re-coupling very difficult.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-2

question: When coupling a triple-trailer rig, what method is used to couple the first trailer to the second trailer?
choice_a: The tractor is backed directly up to the third trailer first
choice_b: The trailers are joined using only safety chains, without a dolly
choice_c: The same method used for coupling doubles
choice_d: A completely separate method requiring two converter dollies at once
explanation: The manual states that after coupling the tractor to the first trailer, the driver moves the converter dolly into position and couples the first trailer to the second trailer using the method for coupling doubles.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-2

question: How does a driver uncouple the third trailer of a completed triple-trailer rig?
choice_a: By lowering the landing gear of the first trailer only
choice_b: By releasing the tractor protection valve first
choice_c: By disconnecting only the safety chains and driving away
choice_d: By pulling the dolly out, then unhitching the dolly using the method for uncoupling doubles
explanation: The excerpt states the third trailer is uncoupled by pulling the dolly out, then unhitching the dolly using the method already described for uncoupling doubles.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-2

question: When inspecting the lower fifth wheel on a combination vehicle, where should the locking jaws be positioned on the kingpin?
choice_a: Around both the head and the shank equally
choice_b: Around the shank of the kingpin, not the head
choice_c: Around the head of the kingpin
choice_d: Position does not matter as long as safety chains are also attached
explanation: The manual's checklist for the lower fifth wheel specifies that locking jaws should be around the shank, not the head, of the kingpin.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-3

question: When inspecting the shut-off valves on a double or triple trailer combination, what position should the shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer be in?
explanation: The manual's inspection checklist states the shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer should be CLOSED.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-3

question: What position should the shut-off valves at the rear of the front trailers be in on a double or triple combination?
explanation: The manual's inspection checklist states the shut-off valves at the rear of the front trailers should be OPEN.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-3

question: During inspection of a double or triple combination, what position should the converter dolly's air tank drain valve be in?
choice_c: It does not matter as long as the petcock is intact
explanation: The manual's inspection checklist specifies the converter dolly air tank drain valve should be CLOSED.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-3

question: When testing the tractor protection valve, within what air pressure range does the manual say the trailer air supply control typically pops out or moves to the emergency position?
explanation: The manual states the trailer air supply control should pop out (or go to the emergency position) when air pressure falls into the range specified by the manufacturer, usually within the range of 20 to 45 psi.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-4

question: What hand control does the manual name for testing the trailer service brakes?
choice_d: The hand control, also called the trolley valve
explanation: The manual describes testing trailer service brakes by applying the trailer brakes with the hand control, also called the trolley valve, if so equipped.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-4

question: What is the first step described for checking that air flows to all trailers on a double or triple combination?
choice_a: Release the converter dolly fifth wheel latch
choice_b: Use the tractor parking brake and/or chock the wheels to hold the vehicle
choice_c: Disconnect the electrical cord from the last trailer
choice_d: Open the emergency line shut-off valve at the front trailer
explanation: The manual's procedure for checking that air flows to all trailers begins by using the tractor parking brake and/or chocking the wheels to hold the vehicle, then waiting for air pressure to reach normal.
source_note: AL CDL Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-4
